newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CALL FOR EXTINGUISHMENT OF NATIVE TITLE ON PASTORAL LEASES
The National Party has announced its official position on the Wik High Court ruling, calling for Native Title on pastoral leases to be extinguished.
The Party also wants the meaning of native title to be clearly defined, and a time limit placed on the process.
Federal Party president, Don McDonald, says uncertainty over the ruling means economic development for the pastoral and mining industries will come to a halt.
Mr McDonald says that would damage aboriginal communities as well and lead to growing social disharmony.
He certainty and security for all landholders must be the minumum outcome.
The Federal Government is yet to detail it's response to the ruling.
GOVTS CRITICISED OVER ABORIGINAL DEATHS IN CUSTODY
Governments have again been criticised for failing to reform the criminal justice system, resulting in the unnecessary incarceration of indigenous people.
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission says the number of deaths in police custody remains relatively low, but Aboriginal deaths in prison are increasing.
An ATSIC report says a stronger emphasis on more punitive approaches to law and order is working against indigenous people, with people being kept in gaol longer.
ATSIC says arrest should be used a last resort, and the problems dealt with by other means.
It says there remain widespread complaints about violent, racist and inappropriate police behaviour.
ATSIC has called for more community policing, a greater political will to decriminalise public drunkenness and sufficient sobering-up facilities.
WA FLOODWATERS RECEDING
In Western Australia's Pilbara region, State Emergency Service workers are assessing flood damage from the air.
Flooding has started to ease after the Ashburton River peaked early this morning at just over 17 metres.
Emergency workers were forced to retreat to safer ground during the night as raging waters spread several hundred metres wide.
Initial reports from the area say the Nanutarra Bridge is still standing although it's not known if it's sustained structural damage.
Rob Te from the SES says he's seen nothing like it since Cyclone Bobby two years ago.
BRYANTS SECURITY NOT TO BLAME FOR RISDON CUTS
Tasmania's Attorney General, Ray Groom says the high security for Martin Bryant had no bearing on cost cutting measures at Risdon Jail.
The government will save almost a quarter of a million dollars by closing the jail's medium security section.
The 23 inmates will be moved into maximum security at Risdon, or relocated to the Hayes Prison Farm in the Derwent Valley.

Mr Groom says the bill for housing Bryant has so far reached about 100-thousand dollars, but the initial high security cost, when there was a 24 hour guard his cell, has now come down quite considerably.
ICE CRACKS COULD BE FROM A NUMBER OF FACTORS
A Hobart glaciologist says cracks found in an ice shelf in Antarctica could have been caused by a number of factors.
Greenpeace says it's filmed large cracks in a number of shelves south of South America, and that their high incidence is a sign of rapid disintegration reflecting the dangers of global warming.
Neil Young from the Antarctic Co-operative Research Centre says that Greenpeace's theory is possible, but he says it's difficult to draw a conclusion.
Mr Young says there has been a warming of up to about three degrees in the area known as the Antarctic peninsula.
But he says a lot of factors need to come into play such as whether the sea ice is present or not, and the variability in terms of climate.
LEADER CONDEMNS PUBLICATION OF WOODS PHOTOS
The leader of the Australian Democrats has condemned the publication of photos of a former liberal front-bencher and his wife in some newspapers today.
Cheryl Kernot says the photos, which show Senator Bob Woods talking to his wife Jane in the garden of their Sydney home, cross the line between what is in the public interest, and what isn't.
Senator Woods is being investigated by Federal Police over the use of his parliamentary expenses, and is the subject of an apprehended violence order application.
Senator Kernot told ABC Radio that the press had been despicable in the way it had pursued people's private lives in this matter.
NEW TAX INCENTIVE FOR FILM INDUSTRY INVESTMENT-REPORT
A new report to the federal government recommends film industry funding be maintained and further investment encouraged with a new tax incentive.
Merchant banker David Gonski compiled the government-commissioned report.
He says despite the air of confidence surrounding the film industry it's still vulnerable.
Mr Gonski says says private investment should be promoted with a new tax concession called the Film Licensed Investment Company.
He also says the current government assistance of 140 million dollars over the next two years should be maintained for at least another five years.
The report's other major recommendation is to change the role of Film Australia from film-maker to commissioning body.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
